sections.h2: Where is the Macomb County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Macomb County Register of Deeds sits within the Clerk's office at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens, MI 48043. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., the phone is 586-469-7953, and the email is registerofdeeds@macombgov.org. Visitors can book an appointment on the county register of deeds page, which also links land record searches, certified copy requests and a status page for documents already sent in.

Macomb is a charter county on the eastern shore of the state, bordering Detroit to the south and Lake St. Clair to the east. The 2020 census counted 881,217 residents, third in Michigan behind Wayne and Oakland, spread across 27 cities, townships and villages. Warren is the largest community and Mount Clemens is the seat. A house in Sterling Heights, St. Clair Shores, Roseville or Romeo records at this one office.

With that many parcels, return times are long: the FAQ says recorded documents come back in roughly 6 to 8 weeks from the recording date. If you need the original quickly after a sale, put a correct RETURN TO name and address on the first page.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Macomb County?
sections.html:
The base charge is $30 per document regardless of page count, a flat fee in place since October 1, 2016 under MCL 600.2567. A document that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3 for each one after the first. The county notes that $4 of the fee goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund, except on fixture filings, liens, state deeds, plats and treasurer reversion documents.

Searching and copying cost extra. In person or by mail, a real estate search carries a $5 minimum, copies are $1 per page, and certifying a copy is $5 per record. Plat copies cost $3.50 for 11 by 17 inches and $4.50 for 18 by 24 inches, with $2.50 shipping if mailed.

sections.h2: Does a Macomb County deed need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
Yes, when it carries a warranty. A warranty deed, any deed with a covenant clause, a land contract and an assignment of land contract must be certified by the county treasurer before the register will record it. The rule comes from MCL 211.135, which asks for proof that taxes on the property were paid for the five years before the instrument's date and that no tax liens or tax titles are held against it.

The same statute exempts quitclaim deeds and other conveyances with no covenants of warranty. It also says a sheriff's deed and a deed of trust given by an assignee or executor need no certificate.

In practice a title company orders the certificate for you. If you are closing without one, call the Macomb County Treasurer at 586-469-5190, which also answers questions about what a property owes. The Land File office at 586-469-5313 can give a legal description, and the local assessor in your city or township can give a taxpayer name and address at no charge.

sections.h2: What does the Macomb County register require on a deed?
sections.html:
The county's recording requirements track MCL 565.201 and the other recording statutes. A deed that misses a point is returned, which holds up a sale. The office stresses these points:

  • Original signatures, with each name typed or printed beneath it and matching the notary's acknowledgment.
  • The grantee's address and the name and address of the person who drafted the document.
  • A notary acknowledgment for any document that conveys or encumbers real estate or cancels a mortgage or lien.
  • A 2.5 inch top margin and half inch side margins on page one. If page one falls short, attach a cover page naming the document.
  • Black ink, 10 point type or larger, white paper of at least 20 pound weight, sized 8.5 by 11 to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Court orders certified and sealed by the clerk of the court.

Where a deed names a deceased owner as grantor, a certified copy of the death certificate must be recorded and referenced. The county says that since September 18, 2018 a death certificate can no longer be attached to another document, so it is recorded as its own item for $30.

sections.h2: How do I add or remove a name on a Macomb County deed?
sections.html:
To add someone, you record a quit claim deed that is typed or in black ink, signed and notarized. The county posts a quit claim deed form on its forms page, and recording costs $30. The office recommends an attorney or someone well versed in real estate matters if the aim is to avoid probate.

To remove a deceased owner, record a certified copy of the death certificate. The cost is $30, and the survivorship wording on the deed controls whether probate is also needed. Staff cannot give legal advice, so a lawyer or title company should confirm which path applies.

A transfer of ownership can also reset the taxable value for the following year under MCL 211.27a, with exceptions for transfers to a spouse and for residential transfers to close family that stay non-commercial. The buyer or new owner must tell the local assessor within 45 days of the transfer.

sections.h2: What happens with a sheriff's deed or foreclosure payoff in Macomb County?
sections.html:
After a mortgage foreclosure sale by advertisement, the person entitled to redeem can ask the register of deeds for a payoff figure. Macomb charges $25 for a payoff letter, paid when you submit the request form, and the letter is ready after 2 business days. The register builds the figure only from the affidavits recorded under the statute, MCL 600.3240, and is not liable for an incorrect determination.

The office also posts a Sheriff's deed payoff letter request form on its page, along with a quit claim deed form and a construction lien form. The county provides those forms without any warranty about their legal effect, so have an attorney review one before you sign it.

Redemption money goes to the register as a certified or cashier's check by 4 p.m. on the last working day of the redemption period. A $5 care and custody fee applies, and it is already inside a figure obtained from the office. The register then issues a letter confirming receipt, and the grantee of the sheriff's deed must draft and record the redemption certificate.

Separately, the county runs a Fraud Notify alerts system for property owners who want to be warned when something is recorded against their name. Signup is linked on the register's page, and it is worth a look before any sale.

faqs.q: How much does Macomb County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $30 per document regardless of pages. If a warranty deed needs a treasurer's tax certificate, add $5 for up to five legal descriptions and $0.20 for each extra description.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get a recorded deed back from the Macomb County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Expect about 6 to 8 weeks from the recording date. Put a correct RETURN TO name and address on the document so it goes to the right person.

faqs.q: Can I check whether my Macomb County document was recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's site has a status of recorded documents page and a land records search, or you can call 586-469-7953. Search and copy fees apply if you request a copy.

faqs.q: Does Macomb County charge transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, in the same way as the rest of Michigan. The county rate is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. The register's FAQ directs transfer tax questions to 586-469-5309.

faqs.q: Do I have to visit the Mount Clemens office to record a deed?
faqs.a: No visit is required. The county FAQ says a completed deed can be mailed in or brought in for recording, and certified copy requests are accepted through the U.S. Mail. Call 586-469-7953 before mailing to confirm the fee.
